newsitem.title: JAPAN: Rightist crashes van at home of Japan PM's brother.
newsitem.headline: Rightist crashes van at home of Japan PM's brother.

text.p: A member of a right-wing group on Monday crashed a van into the front gate of the home of the brother of Japanese Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto, a police spokesman said.
The spokesman told Reuters it was possible there was a political motive for the incident.
He said Daijiro Hashimoto, governor of Kochi Prefecture in the Shikoku island, was at home with his wife when Yuji Morimoto, 27, crashed his van into the front gate of the house.
"The van crashed through the front gate and came to rest in the courtyard of the governor's home. There were no injuries and the man was arrested on the spot," the spokesman said.

He could not confirm media reports that the attack was linked to a speech the governor gave on February 1 in which he questioned whether Japan should keep the song "Kimigayo" (His Majesty's Reign) as Japan's national anthem.
But the spokesman added: "There may be political reasons behind the attack."
Hashimoto"s remarks provoked daily right-wing protests outside his home and office by groups angry at any suggestion that the anthem should be replaced with a modern song.
